newsitem.title: UK: EMS/Mark steady to a touch firmer on crosses.
newsitem.headline: EMS/Mark steady to a touch firmer on crosses.

text.p: 1005 GMT - Mark steady to a touch firmer on European crosses in quiet cross trading. Unexpected 0.2 pct drop in German May industrial output has mixed effect on mark. Dlr/mark stays robust, just shy of latest 40-mth high at 1.7488.

* German May industrial production drops 0.2 pct, much weaker than 0.6 pct rise expected by analysts. Economics ministry adds to gloom by saying it expects to revise May data down further because of additional holidays in May.
* Earlier, German DIW institute says it sees German 1997 and 1998 GDP growth about 2.0 pct and unemployment to rise.
* Traders said weak data ambiguous for mark. Need to keep interest rates low and currency low, offset by concerns about Germany's budget deficit targets and its ability to start EMU.
* Traders eye comments from Tietmeyer late Tuesday that mark is not weak and still merely correcting from 1995 extremes. Analysts said this suggests Buba comfort with mark's decline.

* German opposition SPD's Schroeder says EMU may have to be delayed if stability-oriented start cannot be guaranteed. German CDU's Schaeuble said a French budget deficit of 3.6 pct may be a problem for EMU.
* Mark/lira at 973.80/90 vs 973.10/20 late Tuesday. Mark/Paris at 3.3704/09 vs 3.3701/02 late yesterday.
* BTP/bund spread slides to new record low at 109 bp.
--London Forex Desk +44 171 542 6762
MARK MORNING REPORT

The mark little changed on its European cross rates as traders' attention drifted away from continental Europe to the UK budget, the Thai baht flotation and the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-making meeting.
Analysts said the mark remained subdued, however, with a strong upward bias in dollar/mark persisting and speculation of a timely, broad-based start to the single European currency undaunted.
News of an unexpected 0.2 percent drop in German industrial production in May had little immediate effect, with the impact of weak data seen as slightly ambiguous for the mark.
Analysts polled by Reuters had expected a 0.6 percent rise in output during the month. The German economics ministry said it expected to revise the May data down even further.
"You hardly want to buy marks after the data like this but then again, it does raise questions about meeting EMU targets," said one trader at a major U.S. investment house.
German tax revenue targets are likely to be undershot if growth stays sluggish and this will make it more difficult to meet the EMU budget deficit goals.
Yet, analysts said comments from Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer late Tuesday would keep pressure on the mark.

Tietmeyer said he did not think the mark was weak but, rather, the dollar was strong. He said the mark, which has fallen 3.7 percent this year on a trade weighted basis, was still merely correcting its extreme overvaluation from 1995.

"Tietmeyer can afford to say this (about the mark) given the weakness of the economy and the absence of inflationary pressures. Even though there is an economic recovery underway, there's a long way to go," said Avinash Persaud, head of currency research at JP Morgan in Europe.
Germany's DIW research institute said it sees growth about two percent this year and that jobless will continue to rise.
Germany's failure to meet EMU budgetary targets, meantime, is also potentially ambiguous for the mark.

If the market believes that the political will to start EMU on time will win out regardless of budgetary overshoots then the mark will suffer amid concern about the relative stability of the euro that will replace it.
On the other hand, if signs of budgetary overshoot this year raise concerns among German politicians about the wisdom of starting EMU on time in 1999, then the mark could glean support.
Social Democrat Gerhard Schroeder said EMU may have to be delayed if a stability-oriented start is not guaranteed.

At 0930 GMT, the mark was trading at 973.80/4.10 compared with 973.10/20 late Tuesday. Italian debt markets remained robust, meantime, with the 10-year yield spread between Italy and German narrowing to a new record low at 109 basis points.
Traders said the lira was prone to profit taking, however, as it approached 968 per mark - its notional 2.25 percent limit around the 990 midrate in the European exchange rate mechanism.
Mark/French franc was virtually unchanged at 3.3705/10 compared with 3.3701/02 late yesterday.
--Mike Dolan, London newsroom +44 171 542 6762
